title: Sentence Similarity
summary: Represent sentences as arrays of words.
statement: Represent sentences as arrays of words. Given two sentences and a list of similar word pairs, determine if the sentences are similar by comparing word-by-word using the provided similarity pairs. Sentences are similar if they have the same number of words and corresponding words are similar. Words are always similar to themselves, and similarity is not transitive.
constraints: Sentences are equally long to be similar; listed similarity is symmetric but not transitive.
Each aligned pair must be equal or directly listed as similar.
hints: The rule is an aligned, direct, symmetric relation—not graph reachability.
Normalize each supplied pair into a lookup and test each word position.
Reject unequal lengths; accept position when words equal or either pair orientation exists.
Each sentence position is independent under the contract, so conjunction of direct checks is necessary and sufficient.
editorial: Each sentence position is independent under the contract, so conjunction of direct checks is necessary and sufficient.

tests.explanation: Every aligned pair is equal or directly similar in either listed orientation.
Similarity is not transitive, so great and good are not directly similar.
